quote: A random variable Z is said to be greater than Y in the: (a) Stochastic order (Y <=st Z) if G_Z(z) <= G_Y(z) for all z; (b) Hazard rate order (Y <=hr Z) if h_Z(z) <= h_Y(z) for all z; (c) Mean residual order (Y <=mlr Z) if m_Z(z) <= m_Y(z) for all z; (d) Likelihood ratio order (Y <=lr Z) if g_Z(z)/g_Y(z) is an increasing function of z. The following results (Shaked and Shanthikumar 1994) are well known: Z <=lr Y => Z <=hr Y => Z <=mrl Y => Z <=st Y.
family: Exponentiated Inverse Power Lindley distribution EIPLD(alpha, beta, theta)
